methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Anthro Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by David Mackanic and Joe Papp that has raised $20M to date. The Climate & Energy sector contains one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to apply a reliable peer-median method; only three or more closely aligned datapoints would support that approach.

The stage-progression method is applicable here. Using total raised as a value proxy of $20M and applying a typical Series A to next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $40M. This represents the primary quantitative anchor in the absence of robust peer benchmarking.

The triangulated valuation range supported by this analysis is $34M to $46M, centered on a median of $40M. This range reflects modest sensitivity around the 2.0x step-up assumption. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow peer comparables in the frontier-energy subsector, which limits cross-sectional validation, and the need for additional information on burn rate, runway, and technology differentiation to refine stage-progression assumptions in future rounds.
